previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for bilateral native nephrectomy due to symptomatic polycystic kidney disease causing pain and limited mobility. The surgery was performed successfully, but the postoperative course was complicated by delirium, C. difficile colitis, persistent diarrhea, hypotension during hemodialysis, and postoperative ascites. She was treated with IV and oral vancomycin for C. diff, underwent paracentesis for symptomatic ascites, and was started on midodrine to improve dialysis tolerance. Atenolol was adjusted to be taken later in the day to avoid dialysis-related hypotension. She gradually improved, with resolution of infection and stabilization of volume status. She was discharged home with services on a regimen including oral vancomycin, midodrine, and adjusted antihypertensive and anticoagulant therapy, with follow-up planned for echocardiography and ongoing dialysis management.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Dyspnea-  Patient has had problems with shortness of breath 
since her nephrectomy back in ___.  Her symptoms had worsened 
in recent days so she admitted to ___.  She was ruled out for 
MI and had therapeutic INR making PE unlikely.  Most likely, her 
atrial fibrillation is leading to CHF exacerbations.  Compared 
to previous study in ___, ECHO on ___ showed worsened EF 
(29%), ""mild symmetric left ventricular hypertrophy with 
moderate to severe global biventricular hypokinesis c/w diffuse 
process (toxin, metabolic, tachycardia, etc.). Moderate to 
severe pulmonary artery systolic hypertension and pulmonary 
artery hypertension.""  

While here, she underwent HD on ___ where 3.5L were removed.  
Her symptoms improved dramatically with the initial HD session.  
She underwent UF on ___ and another HD session on ___.  EP 
was consulted re: possibility of tachycardic-induced CHF and 
recommended TEE/cardioversion, which was performed on ___.  
She tolerated the procedure well.  She was comfortable and 
satted well on room air throughout the rest of her 
hospitalization.  

# Atrial fibrillation- Patient has paroxysmal a-fib.  Shes on 
rate and rhythm control with atenolol and amiodarone, 
respectively.  Shes anticoagulated with coumadin 2 mg daily.  Of 
note, her coumadin had been held recently for nephrectomy in 
___. It was restarted in early ___.  Last INR (at HD) was 
3.1, however on admission it was 1.8 so her dose of coumadin was 
increased to 4mg daily.  She remained in an atypical a-flutter 
with a rate of 110-120s while here.  Given the possibility of 
tachycardia-induced heart dysfunction, EP team was consulted.  
They performed TEE/cardioversion on patient (INR was therapeutic 
at the time of procedure).  Upon discharge, she was in sinus 
rhythm and continued on metoprolol, coumadin 3mg daily and 
amiodarone.  

#  PKCD s/p bilateral nephrectomy- Renal was following patient 
while here.  She was dialyzed on ___ and ___ with UF session 
on ___.  She is to continue her outpatient dialysis schedule 
(M, W, F) at ___ on discharge.

chest-pain throughout her hospitalization.  She was continued on 
home medications (atenolol, aspirin, simvastatin) 
 
# HTN-  Patient was continued on atenolol 25 mg PO daily.  Her 
atenolol was switched to metoprolol 25mg PO BID.  Also continued 
on home amlodipine (on non-HD days). BP remained well-controlled 
while here.  Amlodipine was discontinued on discharge.

# H/o C.diff- Patient has recent history of C.diff.  She has 
been on antibiotics prior to admission and was continued on 
current dose of vancomycin (250mg PO TID).  She remained

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with atrial fibrillation, end-stage renal disease on
hemodialysis, now presenting with shortness of breath.  Assess for volume
overload.

COMPARISON:  ___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  There are new bibasilar opacities,
compatible with small bilateral pleural effusion with associated passive
atelectasis.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is suggestive of pericardial
effusion.  The pulmonary vasculature and hilar contours are unchanged and
within normal limits.  There is no pleural effusion or large focal airspace
consolidation, but cannot exclude small early infiltrate.

IMPRESSION:  New bilateral small pleural effusions with atelectasis.  Probable
pericardial effusion.  No definite pneumonia, but cannot exclude superimposed
small infiltrate in the lung bases.  No evidence of fluid overload.

___ at the time of the official interpretation of the study at 11:20AM.

There is no evidence of pulmonary edema.  There is marked worsening of right

cardiomediastinal contours are unchanged.  There is increase in left lower
lobe atelectasis.
